History of the great schools

Ideas, influences and debates.

Lesson 3. Form and person

1 · Lesson

Gestalt psychology was born in Germany with Max Wertheimer, Wolfgang Köhler and Kurt Koffka. Its central idea: we perceive organised wholes, not sums of elements. "The whole is other than the sum of its parts." They described laws of perceptual organisation (proximity, similarity, closure, continuity) and studied problem-solving by insight, sudden understanding.

In the mid-20th century, the humanistic psychology of Carl Rogers and Abraham Maslow presented itself as a "third force" against psychoanalysis and behaviourism. It focused on subjective experience, freedom, personal growth and a therapeutic relationship based on empathy, unconditional acceptance and genuineness.

Gestalt influenced cognitive psychology and visual design. Humanism influenced psychotherapy, education and counselling, and later research has confirmed the importance of the therapeutic relationship in therapy outcomes.

2 · Example

Look at a brand logo made of separate dots that draw a letter. Your brain "closes" the shape and you see the letter, even though there is no continuous line. This is the Gestalt law of closure, used every day in graphic design.

3 · Activity

Look around you for three examples of Gestalt laws (signs, logos, interfaces). For each, say which law applies: proximity, similarity, closure or continuity.
